question.text: A flask contains Hydrogen and Argon in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>1</mn></math> by mass. The temperature of the mixture is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. The ratio of average kinetic energy per molecule of the two gases <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mfrac><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>argon</mi></msub><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>hydrogen</mi></msub></mfrac></mfenced></math> is: (Given : Atomic Weight of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>39</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn></math>)

solution.text:
The formula to calculate the average kinetic energy per molecule of a gas at any temperature T is given by

Kavg=32kBT

where, kB is Boltzmann constant.

From above equation, it can be concluded that the average kinetic energy per molecule is independent of the molecular weight of the gas.

Hence, the required ratio is 1:1.
